mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.5% per annum compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% indicates a rapidly deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 4.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and housing starts (HOUST < 1600 thousand units) indicates a dual deterioration in supply capacity and consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 100 and HOUST < 1600, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.01 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: During active monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates for equities.
failure_condition: During periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly retail sales level above 520,000 million dollars (RSAFS > 520000) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS > 520000, the 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 60% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts level below 1500 thousand units (HOUST < 1500) signals weak residential construction and declining consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1500, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE > 3.8%) and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS < 152000 thousand) indicates a rapidly deteriorating labor market, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 3.8 and PAYEMS < 152000, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.01 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly core inflation rate above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL > 258.5) signals persistent inflationary pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 258.5, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of cases (or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows).
